clue.text: How to move a cask along with one finger

parts.note: to push something is to move it by pressing
a butt is a large cask for wine or ale
on, as in 'move on', means along or forward

explanation.surface: Instructions for shifting a barrel with a single fingertip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to' introduces the recipe: push the butt on. The definition describes a push-button control, worked with one finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A push-button device is operated by pressing a single switch, a job for one fingertip.

clue.text: Youngster would be game to get past a beadle

definitions.text: Youngster would be game to get past a beadle

parts.words: Youngster would be game to get past a beadle
parts.note: a young dog would happily try to slip past the church officer whose old duty was to whip stray dogs out of church

explanation.surface: A plucky child dares to sneak by the parish officer.
explanation.walkthrough: A beadle is a minor parish or church officer; dog-whipping out of church was once among such duties, so the 'youngster' is an animal, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A young dog is the youngster, and 'game' means willing to have a go.

clue.text: Sound advice to the Armada if it had had the armament, ducky !

indicators.note: the opening word says the following phrase is to be spoken out, its pronunciation giving the entry

parts.words: advice to the Armada if it had had the armament
parts.note: the Spanish fleet, if it had had the guns, would have been told to shell Drake, the English admiral

explanation.surface: Wise counsel to the Spanish fleet of 1588, had it carried the guns, with a cheery 'ducky' tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'wise' describing the advice, but it signals a homophone: SHELL DRAKE said aloud gives the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheldrake is a large duck, so 'ducky' here means duck-like, of the duck family.

clue.text: Serving soldier, airborne

definitions.meaning: an officer's personal servant in the British army
a flying man, like the winged creature of the night

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier assigned as an officer's servant has this title; read as bat plus man it is a flying person, the caped comic-strip hero.

clue.text: Henry James's one of nine

definitions.meaning: the title of an 1890 novel by the American writer Henry James
Melpomene, one of the nine Muses, presides over tragedy

explanation.definitionFit: Henry James wrote a novel with this title, and Melpomene among the nine Muses is the patron of tragedy.

clue.text: A manly scent

parts.note: a man's first name, and also the essential oil of roses, a perfume

explanation.surface: Advertising copy for a masculine aftershave.
explanation.walkthrough: The perfume is otto (attar) of roses, hardly manly; the man is a German first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a male forename and a variant of attar, rose oil used in perfume.

clue.text: Dig that tuber !

definitions.meaning: a narrow spade, or to dig with one
a slang word for a potato

explanation.definitionFit: A spud was a narrow digging tool, and in slang it is a potato, the commonest tuber.

clue.text: Balance, I peso

annotationWithheld.why: Balance, I peso: an indicator-less anagram of I PESO (old-style clue, scan confirms the wording); no clue word signals the anagram, so the parse cannot name an indicator

clue.text: " Doth God exact light deny'd?" (Milton)

parts.note: a line from Milton's sonnet on his blindness, with a gap printed where the missing words go

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton's sonnet on his blindness, with a blank to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash after 'exact': the solver supplies the words Milton wrote there, the work of a labourer paid by the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton asks whether God demands a full day's toil from a blind man; work paid by the day fills the gap.

clue.text: That cross look of the screen

definitions.text: That cross look of the screen

parts.words: That cross look of the screen
parts.note: a screen of crisscrossed strips has a pattern of crosses

explanation.surface: A film star's angry glare on the cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross look' suggests an angry face and 'screen' the cinema; the screen is a framework of crossed laths.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a framework of crossed strips used as a screen or trellis.

clue.text: Fold in a box ?

parts.note: a fold found in a box ..., a pair of folds facing each other

explanation.surface: Something creased up inside a cardboard box.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is not a container but a style of skirt fold, the box pleat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold of cloth pressed in place, and the box pleat is one kind.

clue.text: State, as a matter of fact

definitions.text: State, as a matter of fact

parts.words: State, as a matter of fact
parts.note: the condition of being real, what is the case in fact

explanation.surface: Someone saying something in a matter-of-fact way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, to declare; it is a noun, the state of being real.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuality is reality, the condition of existing in fact rather than in theory.

clue.text: Ash as a binding medium

parts.note: the ash tree of Norse myth that binds together heaven, earth and the underworld

explanation.surface: Ash used as a glue or cement in building.
explanation.walkthrough: Ash suggests the residue of fire, a material in mortar; it is the world-tree of Norse myth, whose roots and branches bind the worlds together.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the cosmic ash tree links all the nine worlds, holding the universe together.

clue.text: Lady Headborn with owl

parts.note: the Greek goddess who sprang from the head of Zeus and whose emblem is the owl

explanation.surface: A grand lady with an owl, introduced by a mock-aristocratic title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Headborn' reads as a title of nobility; it describes the goddess born fully armed from her father's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom was born from the head of Zeus and has the owl as her symbol.

clue.text: Brains for contract to control a crossing

parts.note: contract bridge is the card game
the head is where the brains are, and means intelligence

explanation.surface: Someone recruited for their intelligence to handle a deal about a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brains for contract' is a head for bridge, the card game; the military position seized to control a river crossing follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a fortified position on the far side of a river, held to command the crossing.

clue.text: Everything in this garden is far from lovely

definitions.text: Everything in this garden is far from lovely

parts.words: Everything in this garden is far from lovely
parts.note: a turn on the phrase 'everything in the garden is lovely', describing a rowdy place once used for animal baiting

explanation.surface: A complaint that a garden is a mess, twisting the saying that all in the garden is lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: A bear garden was where bears were baited for sport, and the phrase now means a scene of noisy disorder; the four letters fill the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal names the old baiting ground, now a byword for unruly chaos.

clue.text: Ebb with neither ebb nor flow?

definitions.meaning: water going back, as an ebbing tide does; also to row backwards
a still stretch of water off a river, with no current

explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing water is water moving back; a backwater is also a stagnant side channel where the current neither rises nor falls.

clue.text: Hebrews had the measure of a poet-all but

indicators.note: the poet's name is to be taken with one letter removed, almost the whole of it

parts.note: Homer was the poet of the Iliad and Odyssey

explanation.surface: The ancient Hebrews took the measure of a poet, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but' usually drops a last letter; here the poet loses his first, H. The definition reads as 'the measure Hebrews had'.
explanation.definitionFit: The omer was an ancient Hebrew unit of dry capacity, about a tenth of an ephah.

clue.text: Part song

parts.note: a division of a long poem, a part of an epic or song

explanation.surface: A part-song, a choral piece for several voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part song' looks like a musical form; it is a part of a song, a main division of a long poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a principal section of a long poem, from the Italian for song.

clue.text: Devil a bit frayed you are in the country we hear

indicators.note: this phrase says the preceding words are to be spoken, the sound giving the country

parts.words: Devil a bit frayed you are
parts.note: Nick is the Devil, a rag is a frayed bit of cloth, and 'you are' is said as U R

explanation.surface: An insult to a scruffy rascal who is somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick is the Devil; 'a bit frayed' is A RAG; 'you are' run together completes the Central American republic in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaragua is a republic in Central America.

clue.text: Wore an oak ?

parts.note: to sport one's oak is to shut the outer door of college rooms; to sport is also to wear

explanation.surface: Someone dressed up in an oak tree, or in oak leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge the heavy outer door of a student's rooms is the oak, and to 'sport' it is to close it; 'wore' gives the other sense of sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport clothes is to wear them showily, and sporting the oak is the college idiom for shutting the door.

clue.text: Where the Londoner should go to buy meat in bulk

definitions.text: Where the Londoner should go to buy meat in bulk

parts.words: Where the Londoner should go to buy meat in bulk
parts.note: a London street name read as an inexpensive half carcass of meat

explanation.surface: Shopping advice for a Londoner wanting a large cut from the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheapside is a street in the City of London, once its main market; split up it is a side of meat bought at a low price.
explanation.definitionFit: The City street was historically a great market, and its name splits into a bargain side of beef.

clue.text: See 20
A oner in wood

parts.note: a oner is someone or something outstanding, an ace; in wood it is the maple

explanation.surface: Someone who is a unique figure in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: A oner is a first-rate person, an ace; the maple genus spells that as one who aces, so the clue joins top performer and tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, a hardwood.

clue.text: Encourages Humpty Dumpty junior

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme figure was an egg, so his boy is an egg's son

explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them; Humpty Dumpty was an egg, so his heir is an egg's son.

clue.text: Do they remind the contemptible motorist of battles long ago ?

definitions.text: Do they remind the contemptible motorist of battles long ago ?

parts.words: Do they remind the contemptible motorist of battles long ago ?
parts.note: the windscreen blades share their name with the soldiers' slang for Ypres, where the Old Contemptibles fought

explanation.surface: An old soldier at the wheel being reminded of the trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: British troops in the First World War called Ypres in Belgium 'Wipers'; the Old Contemptibles were the regular army sent to France in 1914, so a veteran driver hears the battle in his windscreen blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Windscreen wipers carry the Tommies' nickname for Ypres, scene of three great battles.

clue.text: Shoes to go with hose ?

definitions.meaning: machines that drive water through a hose; also worn with stockings, which are hose

explanation.definitionFit: Light slip-on shoes worn with stockings; and the machines that push water through a fire hose.

clue.text: Can get egg, bread, without a bean

indicators.note: says one can get the entry from the following words, by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A penniless person who can still find egg and bread to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can get' is a loose anagram signal: the letters of EGG and BREAD can be made into the word. 'Without a bean' means penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reduced to poverty has not a penny, not a bean to their name.

clue.text: The doctor is a bore so to speak

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
an awl is a tool that bores holes

explanation.surface: A complaint that the doctor is, so to speak, tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a tedious person; it is a boring tool. 'So to speak' is the definition: to speak in that slow way.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened way of talking, so to drawl is to talk thus.

clue.text: Where we 19, and the tea was beautiful!

definitions.text: Where we 19, and the tea was beautiful!

parts.words: Where we 19, and the tea was beautiful!
parts.note: with the answer to 19 in place, the clue recalls an outing where everyone played games and enjoyed a fine tea

explanation.surface: Fond memories of a day out where the tea was splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the solution to 19 down in the gap: a festive occasion of sport and celebration, a sports day or fete.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive gathering with entertainments, such as a sports gala.

clue.text: Speed in the Greek vale should be moderate

parts.note: Tempe is a famous valley in Thessaly, Greece
rate means speed, as in 'at a great rate'

explanation.surface: A speed limit for the Vale of Tempe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed in the Greek vale' lists both pieces: the valley name followed by a word for speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means restrained, avoiding extremes, which is what moderate describes.

clue.text: Have a fag, mum, while you hear the letter ?

indicators.note: says the preceding words are to be spoken out loud, giving the spelling

parts.note: a fag is British slang for a cigarette, a cig; mum is ma

explanation.surface: A child offering their mother a cigarette while she listens to a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette; CIG MA spoken gives the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: John's crisp intake

indicators.note: read as 'in take': take 'in' away from the name

parts.note: John Ruskin was the Victorian art critic

explanation.surface: John's crunchy snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intake' looks like eating, but split into 'in take' it says take IN away from RUSKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusk is a hard, dry biscuit, a crunchy baked thing.

clue.text: Had a fellow to dine at high table here ?

definitions.text: Had a fellow to dine at high table here ?

parts.note: taken as written
a don is a fellow of a college

parts.words: to dine at high table here
parts.note: a college hall is where dons dine at high table

explanation.surface: A college host invites a fellow to dine at high table in hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Haddon Hall is a medieval manor house in Derbyshire; the clue reads as had a don to dine in hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derbyshire manor house name contains a college fellow dining in hall.
